title: Lisse flat sheaves extended from a locally closed stratum are compact
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, $C$ a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, and $X$ a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. No separatedness of $X$ is assumed. Use ordinary module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] over the constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $g:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and $j:V\hookrightarrow Z$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $L$ be a finite locally constant sheaf of $C$-modules on $V$ [def-constructible-locally-constant], meaning that it is etale locally a constant sheaf with value a finite $C$-module. Assume its geometric stalks [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] are flat $C$-modules, meaning that tensoring with each stalk is exact. Let $j_!$ be ordinary etale extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and $g_*$ closed direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Then $g_*j_!L$, placed in degree zero, is compact [def-pc-compact-object] in $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},C)$. Equivalently the natural map $\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(g_*j_!L,K_i)\to\operatorname{Hom}(g_*j_!L,\bigoplus_iK_i)$ is bijective for every set-indexed family of unbounded complexes $(K_i)$.

source.place: Section 6.4, Example 6.4.1, Lemmas 6.4.4 and 6.4.6, and the last paragraph of the proof of Proposition 6.4.8, printed pp. 48–49. Specialize locally constant perfect values to finite locally constant flat modules in degree zero over the finite ring C. The locally closed extension may be written g_*j_! as well as open_! closed_*; both have the given sheaf on the stratum and zero stalks outside it.

proof.text: Prove compact_of_homEquiv from the defining direct-sum Hom comparison: the direct sum of additive Hom equivalences, the compact source comparison, and the coproduct comparison of the right adjoint are bijective. Naturality identifies their composite with the target comparison. Specialize to additive adjunctions and isomorphisms.

Finite type over the field makes X Noetherian; closed and open strata inherit local Noetherianness and the open stratum is Noetherian as a topological space, hence compact. The structure map of V is finite type. Derived module and sheaf categories have coproducts. The constant-sheaf/derived-global-sections adjunction transports compactness of the degree-zero free rank-one module to the tensor unit on V, since derived global sections preserves coproducts by finite cohomological dimension.

The proved lisse dualizability theorem supplies a dual for L[0]. In a braided monoidal category the duality gives the adjunction tensorLeft L[0] ⊣ tensorLeft D; swapping the pairing also makes tensorLeft D a left adjoint, so it preserves coproducts. The generic compact_of_adjunction helper transports compactness of the unit to L[0] tensor the unit, and the right unitor identifies this with L[0]. This uses the explicit tensor dual rather than specializing the large closed derived internal-Hom definition.

The canonical derived open extension/restriction adjunction transports compactness through j_!, because restriction is itself a left adjoint and preserves coproducts. The canonical closed direct-image/right-adjoint adjunction then transports compactness through Rg_*, using the proved closed-right-adjoint coproduct theorem.

Closed direct image is exact. Its right-derived functor is thus canonically isomorphic to its termwise derived functor. The single-functor comparison isomorphisms for the exact open and closed functors identify the result with (g_* j_! L)[0]. Transport compactness along this explicit composite isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Section 6.4, adjoint compactness argument. Lean uses the canonical constant-sheaf/global-sections, tensor-dual, open-extension/restriction and closed adjunctions. Both auxiliary theorems are proved. The direct tensor-dual argument avoids expensive expansion of the concrete derived internal-Hom definition; no definition or existing statement is changed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q23-ef4388f46 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 7 steps and the statements of all 28 proof_deps, plus Bhatt–Scholze arXiv 1309.1198 §6.4 (printed pp. 47–49: standing assumption, Ex. 6.4.1, Lemmas 6.4.4–6.4.6, Rem. 6.4.7, the end of Prop. 6.4.8). The statement is a faithful specialization: finite ℓ-torsion C, L finite locally constant flat in degree 0, g_*j_! in place of BS's g_!f_*, with the same sheaf. Finite type over k gives Noetherian schemes, so the strata are constructible as Rem. 6.4.7 requires; no separatedness is needed. Small cases: Spec k with L = C works. C = Z/ℓ² with L = Z/ℓ shows the flatness hypothesis is necessary. Empty strata give 0. Steps: (1) finite type, Noetherian, qcqs of j, q and a, from the closed-immersion definition and the cited permanence lemmas, with no affine-intersection assumption. (2) Termwise sums are exact derived coproducts and inverse image preserves them. (3) The finite-type separably-closed dimension node is applied separately to q and a. The qcqs coproduct node then gives that Rq_* and Ra_* preserve sums, and Γ(Spec k) is an equivalence. (4) In the unbounded closed-support triangle, naturality gives a morphism of triangles, and then g^* with the counit g^*g_* ≅ id gives that Rg^! preserves sums. (5) P is finite, hence finitely presented, flat and so projective, hence a retract of C^n; sheafifying the constant presheaves keeps the splitting. (6) Slice restriction of RHom, RHom(C^n, N) = N^n, the explicit retract inverse, and the stalk-conservativity check. (7) The adjunctions plus lem-pur-rhom-global-sections and H^0 of sums in D(C). There is no cycle and there are no new nodes. det-ctf-finite-compact-etale (imported, other unit) is a generalization and was correctly not used as a shortcut; same_as [] is right. No SGA source is cited. tool_uses accepted: the 12 genuinely off-unit generic tools, each used as a black box at its step (the unit has uses []). The declarations for the same-unit lem-pur-rhom-global-sections and the Mathlib-status nodes are redundant but harmless. No fixes.
